help.title: How to command
help.talk.body: You are Hammer. You never act on a unit directly: you call a station on the radio and it decides how to carry out the order. Type a call in the box and send it (Enter, or the Send button), or hold the microphone button (on a keyboard, the ` key), speak, and release: the call is sent as soon as it is transcribed. Picking a squad on the map, then a point, then Hold, Move or Attack writes the call and sends it for you; with a squad picked, a spoken order that names nobody goes to it. On a keyboard, Up and Down in the box bring back earlier calls. Building and buying you do yourself, from the build panel, at once and without a call. Call Anvil, your operator, for anything else that is not one squad's job.
help.attack.say: Viper 1, this is Hammer. Attack Foxtrot. Over.
help.upgrade: Give a squad a smarter brain
help.all.say: All stations, this is Hammer. Attack Zulu. Over.
help.strict.1: A callsign and the order are enough, and a callsign that is only spelled or heard roughly right is corrected. With no callsign, Anvil gets the message.
help.strict.2: Every call opens with who you are calling and who you are: "Viper 1, this is Hammer."
help.strict.3: Full procedure: the opening call, and Over or Out at the end. Anything else is refused.
help.more.body: Black ground has never been seen, dim ground was seen earlier, and clear ground is in sight of your troops right now. A match opens with your headquarters alone, and a base usually grows in this order: a power structure, a refinery (its hauler starts bringing gold from the nearest field), a barracks for squads, a works for vehicles and more haulers, a radar for the small map, an airbase for aircraft; a dockyard for boats when you want the sea. The build panel marks the next of these with a brass corner. The sea rig pumps gold for whoever holds it with a boat or an aircraft. You win by destroying the enemy headquarters or by holding more points when the clock runs out.

tut.title: Lesson
tut.learnAbout: A first match with a coach: you give real orders to real squads, against an enemy that waits for you.
tut.againAbout: Five minutes with a coach, in a match of its own.
tut.welcome: You are {me}, the commander. You never move troops yourself: you give orders on the radio, and each squad's leader carries them out.
tut.select: Start a call: click one of your squads, on the map or in the {squads} list.
tutTouch.select: Start a call: tap one of your squads on the map.
tut.order: Now click {first} on the map and choose {hold}: the call is sent at once. You can also just type it: “{squad} hold {firstName}”.
tutTouch.order: Now tap {first} on the map and choose {hold}: the call is sent at once.
tut.answer: {squad} answers “Wilco”: it will do it. Squads answer you on the radio, and call again when they arrive, meet the enemy or take losses.
tut.orders: The three orders all send the squad to the place; they differ in how it behaves. Move: it goes without stopping to fight. Hold: it takes the place and defends it, and stays. Attack: it looks for a fight and chases the enemy, even away from the place. So: Move to get there fast, Hold to take and defend, Attack to destroy. A place is a named point (A · Alpha to Z · Zulu), a bridge, or a house, bunker, grove or rocks you describe, like “the bunker north of Delta”.
tut.fog: The {hauler} loads at the field and unloads at the {refinery}: that is your income, so guard it. Black map was never seen, dim map was seen earlier, bright map is in sight now. Your squads and the points you hold are your eyes.
tut.buy: Building and buying need nobody's leave. Click {unit} on {build}: it joins the line at the {barracks} at once. The {barracks} makes one squad at a time; more wait in its line, and × takes the last one back.
tutTouch.buy: Building and buying need nobody's leave. Open {buildTab} and tap {unit}: it joins the line at the {barracks} at once. The {barracks} makes one squad at a time; more wait in its line, and × takes the last one back.
tut.deploy: The bar fills, the squad walks out of the door of the {barracks}, and {anvil} tells you it is in the field. {anvil}, your operator, also builds and buys when you ask on the radio, or by itself once you hand it the purse or the whole fight (“{anvil}, run the fight”).
tut.upgrade: Each squad's leader is an AI. An upgrade gives it a stronger one: tier 2 for {cost2} gold, tier 3 for {cost3}. Click ▲ beside a squad in the {squads} list. The list shows the new tier.
tutTouch.upgrade: Each squad's leader is an AI. An upgrade gives it a stronger one: tier 2 for {cost2} gold, tier 3 for {cost3}. Open {squads} and tap ▲ beside a squad. The list shows the new tier.
tut.enemy: An enemy squad is coming for {rig}. Once you can see it, it has a name on the map, like “{target}”. Pick a squad, click the enemy, and choose {attack}.
tutTouch.enemy: An enemy squad is coming for {rig}. Once you can see it, it has a name on the map, like “{target}”. Tap a squad, tap the enemy, then {attack}.
tut.voice: You can also talk: hold the microphone (on a keyboard, the ` key), say the order, and let go. “{procedure}” sets how formal a call must be; relaxed needs only a callsign and the order.
tut.win: You win by destroying the enemy headquarters, or by holding more points when the clock runs out. There is more to find: a radar turns the small map on and opens aircraft and your hero; infantry dig in behind sandbags; tanks run down infantry in the open; squads earn ranks by what they destroy; bridges fall and engineers mend them. Help explains each.
help.a.move: To a named point (A · Alpha to Z · Zulu), to a bridge by its name, to a house, bunker, ruin, grove or rocks you describe (“the grove north of Alpha”), to a spot by bearing (“200 metres east of Golf”), and at enemy squads and structures you can see. Click anything on the map to put its name in the radio box. Infantry sent to a house, bunker or ruin go inside it; any squad sent to a grove or rocks takes cover there. The squad's leader chooses the route.
help.q.auto: What can Anvil do without asking me?
help.a.auto: Nothing, until you give it one of two permissions. The purse (“Anvil, buy as you see fit”, or the button in the squad list): Anvil builds the base in its usual order and buys squads on its own, and tells you when each is ready (and of each purchase as it is made, with Radio traffic set to Full). The fight (“Anvil, run the fight”): Anvil also gives the squads their orders. Take either back with “Anvil, stop buying” or “Anvil, I have command”. Without them Anvil spends gold only when you ask it on the radio (“Anvil, build a barracks”). What you build and buy yourself from the panel needs no permission and no call; a squad you select and send by tapping the map (move, hold, attack) goes at once and answers “Wilco”; every other order to a squad goes by radio.
help.q.upgrade: How do I know an upgrade is happening?
help.a.upgrade: Press ▲ on a squad and send the call. The button shows the request while Anvil decides; when the gold is spent, the squad's tier changes in the list (and the log says so when Radio traffic is set to Full). With your own AI key an upgrade gives that squad's leader a stronger model: tier 2 plans further ahead, tier 3 further still. Without a key the leader is a rule brain and an upgrade gives it more initiative: at tier 2 it takes the cover near it, pulls back when its men are shaken and goes for enemies its weapon can hurt; at tier 3 it also comes at a defended point from the side, asks for support when outnumbered and keeps a long weapon at its range.
help.q.speed: Can a match run slower or faster?
help.a.speed: Yes. The speed is chosen on the start screen when you make a match, together with its length and how hard the scripted enemy presses.
help.q.units: What can I build and buy?
help.a.units: Structures first: a power structure, a refinery (it brings a hauler), a barracks for infantry and engineers, a works for vehicles and more haulers, a radar, an airbase for aircraft, a dockyard for boats, and guns, anti-air and walls or fences to defend. Then units. Aegis: commandos, combat engineers, main battle tank, precision rocket launcher, attack helicopter, strike jet, patrol boat, and the Sentinel. Ashfall: militia, rocket team, sappers, technical, drone swarm, prop bomber, speedboat, and the Oracle. A unit's button says which structure it still needs. Losing a structure takes away what it unlocked until you rebuild it. Engineers take over enemy structures.

help.q.orders: What is the difference between Move, Hold and Attack?
help.a.orders: All three send the squad to the place; they differ in how it behaves. Move: it goes without stopping to fight, and does not fire on the enemy headquarters. Hold: it takes the place and defends it, firing at anything in range, and does not leave. Attack: it looks for a fight and chases the enemy, even away from the place. So on a point or a gold field use Hold to capture and keep it (a squad standing on a point alone for 10 seconds captures it; one that chases the enemy may leave too soon); on the enemy headquarters use Attack or Hold, because a squad sent there with Move only stands beside it. Rule of thumb: Move to get there fast, Hold to take and defend, Attack to destroy.

help.q.place: How do I choose where a structure goes?
help.a.place: Press a structure in the build panel and a ghost of it follows your pointer (on a phone, tap the ground to move it). Ground it can stand on is tinted green: open land, clear of what stands there, near your headquarters or a finished structure of your own, so a base grows outward. A dockyard needs the shore. Click green ground, or press Build here, and it starts going up at once: no call, nobody to ask. Anvil tells you when it stands. Escape, or a click outside the map, cancels.
help.q.line: Why did my tank not come out yet?
help.a.line: Each structure makes one unit at a time; the rest wait in its line, and a full line refuses more. Pressing a unit's card buys it at once; a card with a padlock says which structure it still needs and cannot be pressed. The card shows how many are on their way and the first one's time; low power halves the pace. A second works is a second line. Units come out of the door of the structure that made them, and are lost if it falls first. The × beside a unit's card, or on its row in the squad list, takes the last one out and returns the gold not yet spent. New squads gather beside their structure unless you set a rally point: tap a structure and press Rally point, then tap a point, a tech building or a landmark (or say “Anvil, new squads rally at Delta”). They go there and hold it.

help.q.power: What is power, and why did my guns stop firing?
help.a.power: Every structure supplies or uses power; the sidebar shows use against supply. Your headquarters supplies enough for a refinery and a barracks. Past that, build a power structure first. When use is above supply, structures go up and squads deploy at half speed, your defences stop firing and go dark, and the mini map switches off, until you build more power or sell something. The enemy's power structure is worth destroying for the same reason.
help.a.radar: The mini map works while your radar structure stands and has power. It needs the vehicle works, and the airbase needs it. Without it the panel says why: not built, or no power.
help.q.sell: What can I do with a structure of my own?
help.a.sell: Tap it on the map: one menu offers Rally point (where the units it makes gather), Cancel last (the last unit in its line), Repair, and Sell, each with its gold. Each happens at once. Selling gives back half the cost and removes what the structure unlocked. Repairing takes gold as it mends and stops when the structure is whole or the gold runs out. With an engineer squad picked the menu also offers to send them (or say “Viper 3, repair the refinery”): standing beside it and not under fire they mend it over time for no gold, and are free again when it is whole. Only engineers can; the squad says so on the radio if it cannot.
help.q.defences: Why can my squads not shoot a gun down from a distance?
help.a.defences: A defence outranges every ordinary weapon. Each army has one siege unit that outranges defences (the rocket launcher, or the rocket team against structures); send it with another squad to spot the target, or cut the enemy's power so its guns fall silent.

help.take: The Oracle takes over an enemy vehicle
help.a.heroes: Each army has one: a single soldier with a leader of its own, bought from Anvil once a barracks, a vehicle works and a radar stand (“Anvil, buy the hero”). Only one can be alive at a time, and each side is told once, by Anvil, when a hero takes the field or falls. The Sentinel (callsign Ghost) is seen only from close by until it fires and sets demolition charges on an enemy structure, a bridge or the enemy headquarters; a defence finds it. The Oracle (callsign Raven) passes for a bystander at a distance, shakes the nerve of squads near it, and takes over one enemy vehicle squad for as long as it lives and stays near it: kill the Oracle or drive it off and the vehicle is yours again. With a hero picked, tap a structure, a bridge or an enemy vehicle and the menu offers its order. A hero on such a task keeps going under fire unless it is pinned.
help.q.digIn: How do sandbags work, and what do tanks do to infantry?
help.a.digIn: Tell an infantry squad to dig in (“Viper 2, dig in”), or pick the squad and tap it again for the Dig in button. After a few seconds standing still without being shot at, it builds a sandbag position facing the nearest enemy in sight, or the nearest point you do not hold. The position covers its men from that front only, so a flank still works, against you and for you. Heavy weapons knock sandbags down and a vehicle driving over them flattens them. Each squad can build two, and a position has a name you can send squads to. A tank that drives through infantry in the open runs them down, one man each pass; men inside a building, behind standing sandbags or in a grove are safe, and steady squads step out of the way.
help.q.ranks: What are the silver stars beside a squad?
help.a.ranks: A rank the squad earned by what it destroyed: one star (Seasoned) at three times its own cost, a star over a bar (Elite) at six times. A ranked squad shoots straighter and keeps its nerve longer, and an Elite squad mends its wounds out of combat. This is apart from the brass chevrons of the brain tier, which you buy; a squad keeps its rank when you upgrade its brain.

tut.cover: Cover decides fights. A squad holding a place uses the cover it finds there; the shield beside its name shows how much. For more, pick a squad, click a building and choose {cover}.
tut.power: Now your base. A match opens with the headquarters alone. Under the map, on {structures}, click {power}: a ghost of it follows the pointer. Click green ground and it starts going up there at once. Everything else you build uses power: run short and building slows, the defences fall silent and the radar goes dark.
tutTouch.power: Now your base. A match opens with the headquarters alone. Open {buildTab}, then {structures}, and tap {power}: a ghost of it appears on the map. Tap green ground to move it, then {buildHere}: it starts going up at once. Everything else you build uses power: run short and building slows, the defences fall silent and the radar goes dark.
help.q.cover: What is cover, and how do I use it?
help.a.cover: A squad in cover is hit far less. One told to hold a place takes the cover it finds there by itself: inside a house, bunker or ruin with room for it, or close behind a grove, rocks or a wall; the shield beside its name on the map shows how much. To choose the cover yourself, pick a squad, tap the building and press Take cover. A squad told to hold a spot you gave by distance (“150 metres north of Delta”) stands on that ground and goes into no building. A building under heavy fire comes down, and whoever was inside is out and shaken.
help.q.bridges: How do bridges, water and mountains work?
help.a.bridges: Water stops land units except at a bridge, mountains stop them, and ice is slow and open. A squad told to attack a bridge shoots it from the bank; when a bridge falls, everything on it is lost, and the far bank can be reached only by another bridge, by boat or by air. Engineers sent to a fallen or damaged bridge mend it.
help.q.tech: What are the buildings that belong to nobody?
help.a.tech: Tech buildings stand on the map from the start: the Assay Office pays gold while you hold it, the Field Clinic heals infantry near it, the Service Yard mends vehicles near it. Send engineers to take one (pick them, tap the building, Take over); the enemy can take it back the same way, and it can be destroyed. Each has a name you can use as a place, also for a rally point.
help.a.cues: Anvil. The plain news of your base comes as short fixed lines in Anvil's voice, marked with a small beacon in the log: construction complete, a squad in the field, not enough gold, the line is full, low power and power restored, the base or a hauler under attack, a structure lost, taken or sold, repairs stopped for want of gold, a unit lost with the structure that was making it, a hero in the field or down. They cost no AI and wake nobody. Settings has a switch to have them written only, not spoken.
placer.run: Runs {run}. Turn it with R, the wheel or the button.
help.q.turn: Can I turn a wall before I place it?
help.a.turn: Yes. While a wall or fence follows your pointer, press R or roll the wheel (on a phone, the Turn button beside Build here): the run turns through north to south, east to west and the two diagonals. Each segment shows green or red, and the whole run must fit.
squadNet.empty: What your squads and Anvil say to each other is written here. It is never spoken aloud.
traffic.about: Quiet: only what needs you, and the answers to your own orders. Normal: also one line for each new contact and each objective reached. Full: everything. A squad you ordered yourself always reports to you.
help.q.nets: Why are there two nets, and how do I hear less?
help.a.nets: The command net carries what is said to you and by you: your orders and their answers, Anvil's news of the base and of a fight, and the game's own lines. What squads and Anvil say among themselves is on the squad net, the tab beside it: it is written, never spoken. Squads that move together report an enemy or an arrival once, not once each, and Anvil sums a fight up for you instead of passing every report on. In Settings (⚙), Radio traffic sets how much reaches the command net and your ears: Quiet (base under attack, a squad or a point lost or taken, something ready, answers to your orders), Normal (also each new contact and each objective reached) or Full (everything, the squad net too). A squad you ordered yourself by radio keeps answering you and reporting contact at every level.
help.strike: Send a strike aircraft at a target
help.a.planes: The airbase also makes a strike aircraft: the Strike jet for Aegis, the Prop bomber for Ashfall, callsign Comet. It stands at the airbase and holds no ground. Give it a target (“Comet 1, attack Zulu”, an enemy structure, a bridge, “Target 3”): it flies straight there over everything, drops all its bombs in one pass, flies home and rearms before it can go again. A structure, a bridge, a building, the enemy headquarters or an enemy squad that stays in sight is flown at again until it is gone; open ground gets one pass. “Comet 1, move to Delta” is a flight over the place and back, to look: you cannot order a strike on a structure your side has never seen. “Comet 1, return to base” calls it off. It cannot hold, capture or hit aircraft. Anti-air defences and most infantry shoot at it on the way, so strike what cannot shoot up, or take out the anti-air first. If your last airbase falls, the planes standing on it are lost with it.
